reader_summary.headline: I discovered Coifin earlier this year when I asked Twitter for the best Bloomberg alternative.
reader_summary.overview: I discovered Coifin earlier this year when I asked Twitter for the best Bloomberg alternative, and the overwhelming winner was an intriguing new product called Coifin. Coifin is a web-based platform that lets you analyze stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, and other assets all in one place. I now use it daily to track what's going on in the market, and I think if you try it, you will too.

key_points.text: Coifin has tons of high-quality data, powerful functionality, and a nice, clean interface.

positions.commentary: The speaker expresses strong confidence in DoorDash's founder, Tony, stating they would never bet against him.
The speaker uses Airbnb as an example to explain how marketplace dynamics shift between supply and demand sides over time.
The speaker highlights Fair's CEO Max Roden as an example of a leader who successfully improved his people management skills to scale.

thesis: This episode argues that growth investing success is driven by founders with exceptional clarity of thought, grit, and determination, rather than just market dynamics. The speaker suggests that identifying leaders who can scale their people and navigate capital-intensive environments is a key investment filter.

claims.claim: The speaker expresses strong confidence in DoorDash's founder, Tony, stating they would never bet against him.
claims.quote: DoorDash has gone to hell and back. And I would never bet against Tony. I'd say the same about Rappi, the Latin American company, which is in Stacupas

claims.claim: The speaker uses Airbnb as an example to explain how marketplace dynamics shift between supply and demand sides over time.
claims.quote: So let's look at Airbnb. You have the host and the guest. Initially, the guests were actually easier to get because when they targeted events, so their famous story is the road airline design conference or there was a design conference going on in San Francisco and all the hotels were sold out.

claims.claim: The speaker cites Brex founders as an example of clarity of thought regarding whether a company can become a billion-dollar entity.
claims.quote: I usually refer to the Brex founders for this example. So the Brex founders went through Weiss in Winter 17 and second or third week into the badge. They had this idea of Brex, which is corporate credit card for startups.

claims.claim: The speaker highlights Fair's CEO Max Roden as an example of a leader who successfully improved his people management skills to scale.
claims.quote: Fair, the company Fair, the CEO Max Road, is an example. Like, if you look at his resume, tremendous background, he was the GM of Caviar, launched Square Cash, and Fair is like a marketplace marketplace that connects makers and retailers.

claims.claim: The speaker praises Rappi's founders for having unparalleled grit and determination despite operating in a capital-intensive environment.
claims.quote: I'd say the same about Rappi, the Latin American company, which is in Stacupas, I mean, they don't even have a strong venture capital market in LADAM, and they're here they are building a capital intensive company. But my God, their grit and determination is unparalleled.
